text:
Predicates:
Student(x) ::: x is a student.
WorkInLibrary(x) ::: x works in the library.
PartTimeJob(x) ::: x has a part-time job offered by the university.
Course(x, y) ::: x takes course y.
Department(x, y) ::: x is from department y.
Instructor(x, y) ::: x instructs y.
Lab(x) ::: x works in the lab.
HasPartTimeJob(x) ::: x has a part-time job offered by the university.
WorksInLab(x) ::: x works in the lab.
Questioned(x) ::: x is the subject of the question.
HasPartTimeJobOffered(x) ::: x has a part-time job offered by the university.
WorksInLab(x) ::: x works in the lab.

Premises:
¬∃x (Student(x) ∧ WorkInLibrary(x) ∧ PartTimeJob(x)) ::: No students who work in the library are from the computer science department.
∀x (PartTimeJob(x) ∧ OfferedByUniversity(x) → WorkInLibrary(x)) ::: All students who have part-time jobs offered by the university work in the library.
∀x (Course(x, database) → Department(x, computer_science)) ::: All students who take the database course are from the computer science department.
∀x (Instructor(x, y) → Course(y, database)) ::: All students instructed by professor David are taking the database course.
∀x (WorksInLab(x) → Instructor(x, david)) ::: All students working in the lab are instructed by professor David.
James ::: James is a student working in the lab.
Jack ::: Jack neither has a part-time job offered by the university nor works in the lab.

Conclusion:
¬HasPartTimeJobOffered(James) ::: James does not have a part-time job offered by the university.
